q: In what year did Diego Maradona score his “Hand of God” goal against England?
hint: For scale: England won its only men’s World Cup in 1966.
clue: Argentina first won the World Cup, on home soil, in 1978.
card: Four minutes later he scored again after dribbling past half the England team, a goal later voted the best of the century.

q: In what year did Tokyo first host the Summer Olympics, the first Games held in Asia?
hint: For scale: London hosted the first Summer Olympics after World War II, in 1948.
clue: Munich hosted the Summer Olympics in 1972.
card: Japan opened its first bullet train line just nine days before the opening ceremony.

q: How many seconds did Usain Bolt take to run his 2009 world-record {=100 m}?
hint: For scale: a fit adult jogging takes about 25 seconds to cover {100 m}.
clue: Bolt’s {=200 m} world record, set at the same championships, took 19.19 seconds.
card: He set it in Berlin, at the very same race where he reached his famous top speed.

q: In the NBA, how far is the free-throw line from the backboard?
hint: For scale: the rim hangs {3.05 m} above the floor.
clue: A giraffe can stand about {5.5 m} tall.
card: Free throws are worth one point each, and the shooter must stay behind the line until the ball hits the rim.

q: How many players does each kabaddi team have on the court at once?
hint: For scale: a basketball team has five players on the court.
clue: A volleyball team has six players on the court.
card: Raiders must chant “kabaddi” without taking a breath while they try to tag opponents and return home.

q: In what year was the first men’s Cricket World Cup played?
hint: For scale: the first Rugby World Cup was played in 1987.
clue: Moscow hosted the Summer Olympics in 1980.
card: The West Indies won that first tournament in England, and matches were 60 overs a side.

q: How high is a table tennis net?
hint: For scale: a table tennis ball is {40 mm} across.
clue: An ice hockey puck is {7.6 cm} across.
card: The net also hangs out {15.25 cm} beyond each side of the table.

q: How long is Studio Ghibli’s My Neighbor Totoro (1988), in minutes?
hint: For scale: Disney’s Frozen (2013) runs 102 minutes.
clue: Pixar’s Up (2009) runs 96 minutes.
card: The big gray forest spirit became Studio Ghibli’s logo.

q: How many episodes of the original Naruto anime series were made?
hint: For scale: Breaking Bad ran for 62 episodes.
clue: Dragon Ball Z ran for 291 episodes.
card: The story continued in a sequel series, Naruto: Shippuden, which picked up the hero a few years older.

q: In what year was the Bollywood romance Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge released?
hint: For scale: the Bollywood classic Sholay came out in 1975.
clue: Shah Rukh Khan’s Devdas came out in 2002.
card: A Mumbai cinema kept showing it for over two decades, the longest run in Indian film history.

q: How long is Christopher Nolan’s Inception (2010), in minutes?
hint: For scale: Titanic (1997) runs 195 minutes.
clue: Jurassic Park (1993) runs 127 minutes.
card: The spinning-top ending was so debated that Nolan’s own crew asked him what it meant.

q: In what year was Akira Kurosawa’s Seven Samurai released?
hint: For scale: Hollywood’s Casablanca came out in 1942.
clue: Kurosawa’s samurai film Yojimbo came out in 1961.
card: Hollywood remade it as the Western The Magnificent Seven.

q: How many episodes of the anime Death Note were made?
hint: For scale: Breaking Bad ran for 62 episodes.
clue: Stranger Things ran for 42 episodes.
card: The series began as a manga about a student who finds a notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it.

q: In what year did the Pokémon anime first air in Japan?
hint: For scale: Dragon Ball Z first aired in 1989.
clue: The Sailor Moon anime first aired in 1992.
card: Pikachu was not originally planned as the star; he was picked because he appealed to a wide audience.

q: In what year was reggae star Bob Marley born?
hint: For scale: Elvis Presley was born in 1935.
clue: John Lennon was born in 1940.
card: He was born in the small village of Nine Mile in Jamaica, where he is also buried.

q: How long is the original “Despacito” by Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee, in seconds?
hint: For scale: the Beatles’ “Hey Jude” runs 431 seconds.
clue: Michael Jackson’s “Billie Jean” runs 294 seconds.
card: Its music video became the first on YouTube to pass three billion views.

q: How many strings does a traditional Japanese koto have?
hint: For scale: a standard guitar has six strings.
clue: A mandolin has eight strings.
card: Players tune each string by moving a small bridge under it, and pluck with picks worn on three fingers.

q: In what year did Ricky Martin release “Livin’ la Vida Loca”?
hint: For scale: Shakira’s “Hips Don’t Lie” came out in 2006.
clue: Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You” came out in 1994.
card: It was one of the first hit songs recorded and mixed entirely on a computer, using Pro Tools.

q: In what year was Ludwig van Beethoven born?
hint: For scale: Johann Sebastian Bach died in 1750.
clue: Mozart was born in 1756.
card: He kept composing after losing his hearing, and could not hear the audience cheer at the premiere of his Ninth Symphony.

q: How long is PSY’s “Gangnam Style,” in seconds?
hint: For scale: Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody” runs 355 seconds.
clue: Michael Jackson’s “Beat It” runs about 258 seconds.
card: Gangnam is a wealthy district of Seoul, and the song pokes fun at its flashy lifestyle.

q: How many symphonies did Joseph Haydn write, by the standard numbering?
hint: For scale: Mozart wrote 41 numbered symphonies.
clue: A standard piano has 88 keys.
card: His “Surprise” Symphony got its nickname from a sudden loud chord in a quiet slow movement.

q: How many cards are in a deck of hanafuda, the Japanese flower cards?
hint: For scale: a tarot deck has 78 cards.
clue: A Pokémon Trading Card Game deck has 60 cards.
card: Nintendo was founded in 1889 in Kyoto to make hanafuda cards, long before it made video games.

q: How many intersections are there on a standard full-size Go board?
hint: For scale: a chessboard has 64 squares.
clue: A Scrabble board has 225 squares.
card: Go stones are played on the points where the lines cross, not inside the squares.

q: In what year were the first Pokémon games, Red and Green, released in Japan?
hint: For scale: Super Mario Bros. came out in 1985.
clue: Nintendo’s Super Famicom console came out in Japan in 1990.
card: Creator Satoshi Tajiri was inspired by his childhood hobby of collecting insects.

q: In what year did Momofuku Ando sell the first instant noodles, Chicken Ramen?
hint: For scale: the Slinky went on sale in 1945.
clue: Nutella first went on sale in 1964.
card: Ando later invented Cup Noodles too, after seeing people break noodle blocks into cups.

q: How tall is a standard LEGO minifigure?
hint: For scale: a classic Barbie doll is about {29 cm} tall.
clue: A standard 2×4 LEGO brick is {3.2 cm} long.
card: The first minifigures of 1978 had smiling faces and no printed noses.

q: How hot is the oven for a traditional Neapolitan pizza, by the official rules?
hint: For scale: a home kitchen oven tops out around {250 °C}.
clue: Lead melts at {327 °C}.
card: At that heat the pizza bakes in about a minute and a half.

q: In what year did Alexey Pajitnov create Tetris in Moscow?
hint: For scale: Pong arrived in arcades in 1972.
clue: Space Invaders arrived in arcades in 1978.
card: The name mixes “tetra,” Greek for four, with tennis, Pajitnov’s favorite sport.

q: How tall is the minaret of the Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca?
hint: For scale: the Great Pyramid of Giza was {146 m} tall when finished.
clue: London’s Gherkin skyscraper is {180 m} tall.
card: At night a laser on top shines a beam toward Mecca.

q: How long is the main span of the Bosphorus Bridge in Istanbul?
hint: For scale: the Brooklyn Bridge’s main span is {486 m}.
clue: The Golden Gate Bridge’s main span is {1,280 m}.
card: It links Europe and Asia, and each year runners cross it between the two continents during the Istanbul Marathon.

q: How tall is the Qutb Minar in Delhi?
hint: For scale: the Arc de Triomphe in Paris is {50 m} tall.
clue: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is about {56 m} tall.
card: Building began around 1199, and the tower has 379 steps inside.

q: How long is the Rio–Niterói Bridge across Guanabara Bay in Brazil?
hint: For scale: the Channel Tunnel is about {50 km} long.
clue: The Øresund Bridge between Denmark and Sweden is about {7.8 km} long.
card: Its central span rises high enough for ships to sail under it into Rio’s harbor.

q: How tall is Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur, including its spire?
hint: For scale: Kuala Lumpur’s Petronas Towers are {452 m} tall.
clue: Taipei 101 in Taiwan is {508 m} tall.
card: Its name comes from “merdeka,” Malay for independence, and it stands beside the stadium where Malaysia’s independence was declared.

q: How many steps lead up to the Batu Caves temple in Malaysia?
hint: For scale: Rome’s Spanish Steps have 135 steps.
clue: There are 334 steps to the belfry of London’s Elizabeth Tower.
card: The stairs were painted in bright rainbow colors in 2018.

q: How high above sea level is Machu Picchu in Peru?
hint: For scale: Mount Fuji rises {3,776 m} above sea level.
clue: The nearby city of Cusco sits about {3,400 m} above sea level.
card: The Inca built it without mortar, cutting stones to fit so tightly that a knife blade cannot slip between them.

q: In what year did India’s Chandrayaan-3 land near the Moon’s south pole?
hint: For scale: NASA’s Curiosity rover landed on Mars in 2012.
clue: SpaceX first landed a rocket booster back on Earth in 2015.
card: India became the first country to land near the Moon’s south pole.

q: In what year did Yang Liwei become China’s first astronaut in space?
hint: For scale: Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space in 1961.
clue: A Space Shuttle first flew into space in 1981.
card: His Shenzhou 5 capsule circled Earth 14 times before landing in Inner Mongolia.

q: How wide is Titan, Saturn’s largest moon?
hint: For scale: Earth’s Moon is {3,474 km} wide.
clue: Mars is {6,779 km} wide.
card: Titan is bigger than the planet Mercury, and it has lakes and rivers of liquid methane.

q: How long is a year on Venus, counted in Earth days?
hint: For scale: Mercury circles the Sun in 88 days.
clue: Earth takes about 365 days.
card: A Venus day is longer than its year: it spins so slowly that one turn takes longer than a trip around the Sun.

q: How wide is Ceres, the largest object in the asteroid belt?
hint: For scale: Pluto is {2,377 km} wide.
clue: Japan’s main island, Honshu, is about {1,300 km} long.
card: Ceres was found in 1801 and was called a planet for about half a century.

q: In what year did Nicolaus Copernicus publish his book putting the Sun at the center of the Solar System?
hint: For scale: Galileo discovered Jupiter’s four largest moons in 1610.
clue: Leonardo da Vinci died in 1519.
card: Legend says Copernicus was handed a printed copy on his deathbed.

q: How wide is the dish of FAST, China’s giant radio telescope?
hint: For scale: Puerto Rico’s former Arecibo dish was {305 m} wide.
clue: The Eiffel Tower is {330 m} tall.
card: It sits in a natural limestone bowl in Guizhou province, and its nickname is Tianyan, the “Eye of Heaven.”

q: How many chromosomes are in a typical chimpanzee body cell?
hint: For scale: a dog cell holds 78 chromosomes.
clue: A cat cell holds 38 chromosomes.
card: Two ape chromosomes fused long ago to form human chromosome 2.

q: How far does an Arctic tern fly in a typical year of migration?
hint: For scale: a round trip between London and Sydney is about {34,000 km}.
clue: Earth’s equator is about {40,000 km} around.
card: Arctic terns see two summers a year, one near each pole, so they get more daylight than any other animal.

q: How wide can the flower of Rafflesia arnoldii, the largest single flower, grow?
hint: For scale: a big sunflower head is about {30 cm} across.
clue: A typical adult bicycle wheel is about {70 cm} across.
card: It smells of rotting meat to attract flies, earning it the name “corpse flower.”

q: How far does Australia’s Great Barrier Reef stretch?
hint: For scale: the River Nile runs about {6,650 km}.
clue: Italy is about {1,200 km} long from the Alps to its southern tip.
card: It is the world’s largest structure built by living things and can be seen from space.

q: How many vertebrae are in an owl’s neck?
hint: For scale: humans and giraffes both have 7 neck vertebrae.
clue: A typical cat has 18 toes.
card: The extra bones let an owl turn its head about 270 degrees.

q: How many chambers does a frog’s heart have?
hint: For scale: a fish heart has two chambers.
clue: The human heart has four chambers.
card: Frogs can also breathe through their skin, which is why it must stay moist.

q: How much does an adult’s fingernail grow in a month, on average?
hint: For scale: a toenail grows about {1.6 mm} a month.
clue: A standard pencil lead is about {2 mm} thick.
card: Nails on your dominant hand tend to grow a bit faster.

q: In what year did Japan’s Meiji Restoration return power to the emperor?
hint: For scale: Napoleon was defeated at Waterloo in 1815.
clue: London’s first Underground line opened in 1863.
card: The emperor moved from Kyoto to Edo, which was renamed Tokyo, meaning “eastern capital.”

q: In what year did Mahatma Gandhi lead the Salt March in India?
hint: For scale: India gained independence in 1947.
clue: Tutankhamun’s tomb was discovered in 1922.
card: He walked about {390 km} to the sea to make salt in defiance of British law.

q: In what year did Nelson Mandela become president of South Africa?
hint: For scale: the Chernobyl disaster happened in 1986.
clue: The Berlin Wall fell in 1989.
card: He had spent 27 years in prison before his release.

q: In what year was Genghis Khan proclaimed ruler of all the Mongols?
hint: For scale: construction of the Leaning Tower of Pisa began in 1173.
clue: The Magna Carta was sealed in 1215.
card: His empire later became the largest connected land empire in history.

q: In what year did Vasco da Gama first reach India by sea?
hint: For scale: the Ottoman Empire captured Constantinople in 1453.
clue: Columbus first reached the Americas in 1492.
card: His route around Africa’s Cape of Good Hope opened the first all-sea trade route from Europe to Asia.

q: How many steps climb each of the four sides of El Castillo, the great pyramid at Chichén Itzá?
hint: For scale: Rome’s Spanish Steps have 135 steps.
clue: A standard tarot deck has 78 cards.
card: At the equinoxes, the late sun casts a shadow that looks like a serpent sliding down the stairs.

q: How many years did Japan’s Edo period, under the Tokugawa shoguns, last?
hint: For scale: the Hundred Years’ War actually lasted 116 years.
clue: The Romanov family ruled Russia for over 300 years.
card: For most of it Japan limited contact with foreigners, allowing only a few Dutch and Chinese traders in Nagasaki.

q: How tall is Bagger 293, the giant German mining excavator?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 747-8 is {76 m} long.
clue: A soccer pitch is about {105 m} long.
card: It is one of the heaviest land vehicles ever built, yet it can crawl along on its own tracks.

q: What was the wingspan of the Antonov An-225 Mriya, the world’s largest cargo plane?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 737-800 spans {35.8 m}.
clue: An Airbus A380 spans {79.8 m}.
card: Only one was ever completed; it was originally built to carry the Soviet space shuttle Buran on its back.

q: What speed did Japan’s L0 maglev train reach in its 2015 world-record run?
hint: For scale: a Formula One car tops out around {350 km/h}.
clue: A typical jet airliner cruises at about {900 km/h}.
card: It floats about {10 cm} above its guideway on magnets once it gets up to speed.

q: In what year did Nokia release its famously tough 3310 phone?
hint: For scale: the first text message was sent in 1992.
clue: The first iPhone came out in 2007.
card: It came with the game Snake II, and more than 120 million were sold.

q: What was the top speed of Karl Benz’s first Motorwagen?
hint: For scale: a person walks at about {5 km/h}.
clue: A relaxed city cyclist rides at about {20 km/h}.
card: In 1888 his wife Bertha drove one over {100 km} to her mother’s house, the first long car trip.

q: How tall is Ain Dubai, the giant Ferris wheel in Dubai?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is {330 m} tall.
clue: London’s Shard skyscraper is {310 m} tall.
card: It is nearly twice as tall as the London Eye.

q: How long is the classic 1957 Fiat 500 car?
hint: For scale: a typical family car is about {4.5 m} long.
clue: A Smart Fortwo city car is about {2.7 m} long.
card: Its tiny two-cylinder engine sat in the back, under a lid at the rear.

q: How long is Egypt’s Suez Canal?
hint: For scale: the Channel Tunnel is about {50 km} long.
clue: Germany’s Kiel Canal is about {98 km} long.
card: It has no locks, because the Mediterranean and the Red Sea are at nearly the same level.

q: How tall is Aconcagua in Argentina, the highest mountain in the Americas?
hint: For scale: Mont Blanc, the highest peak in the Alps, is {4,806 m} tall.
clue: Denali in Alaska is {6,190 m} tall.
card: It is the highest mountain anywhere outside Asia.

q: How many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of India’s constitution?
hint: For scale: the United Nations has six official languages.
clue: The European Union has 24 official languages.
card: Indian banknotes print their value in many of these languages on a panel on the back.

q: How long is China’s Yangtze River?
hint: For scale: the Danube runs about {2,850 km}.
clue: The Trans-Siberian Railway is about {9,289 km} long.
card: It is the longest river that flows entirely within one country.

q: How tall is Table Mountain above Cape Town in South Africa?
hint: For scale: Mount Fuji is {3,776 m} tall.
clue: The Burj Khalifa is {828 m} tall.
card: Its flat top is often covered by a cloud locals call the “tablecloth.”

q: How many letters are in the Russian alphabet?
hint: For scale: the English alphabet has 26 letters.
clue: The Spanish alphabet has 27 letters.
card: Two of its letters, the hard and soft signs, have no sound of their own.

q: How large is Brazil?
hint: For scale: India covers about {3,287,000 sq km}.
clue: Canada covers about {9,985,000 sq km}.
card: Brazil borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
